notions.texte: It's the place where students go to wash their hands.
It's the place where students go to play and practise sports.
It's the work place of the secretary.
It's the garden of a school. It's the place where students go to grow vegetables.
I like speaking English.
I like English.
I dislike cleaning the board.
I dislike dogs.

La suite des lieux de l'école. Même exercice qu'en Session 1 : c'est la définition en anglais qu'il faut savoir redire. Word — Definition A toilet — It's the place where students go to wash their hands. A playground — It's the place where students go to play and practise sports. A secretary's office — It's the work place of the secretary. A school garden — It's the garden of a school. It's the place where students go to grow vegetables.
Le bouton 🔊 de chaque ligne lit le mot et sa définition en anglais. Attention à playground et secretary, qui ne se prononcent pas comme ils s'écrivent.
Dire ce qu'on aime et ce qu'on n'aime pas. Toute la leçon tient dans une seule règle, à appliquer deux fois.
Après like ou dislike, deux constructions seulement : like / dislike + verbe + -ING like / dislike + nom
Construction — Example like + V-ing — I like speaking English. like + noun — I like English.
Construction — Example dislike + V-ing — I dislike cleaning the board. dislike + noun — I dislike dogs.

notions.titre: La faute à ne pas faire
notions.texte: On ne dit jamais « I like to speak English » dans cette leçon, ni « I like speak English ». Après like, le verbe prend -ing : speaking, cleaning, playing, reading.

Prends les lieux de la Session 1 et 2, et fais quatre phrases : I like going to the library. (V-ing) I like the school garden. (nom) I dislike cleaning the playground. (V-ing) I dislike the canteen. (nom)
Cherche d'abord seule, à voix haute si tu peux. Ensuite, ouvre la correction.

Trouve le lieu qui correspond à la définition. It's the place where students go to play and practise sports. → … It's the work place of the secretary. → … It's the place where students go to grow vegetables. → … It's the place where students go to wash their hands. → … A secretary's office A school garden

Mets le verbe à la forme -ing. I like (play) … football. I dislike (clean) … the classroom. She likes (read) … books in the library. I like (dance) …. He dislikes (swim) …. I like (write) … stories. Deux règles d'orthographe : le e final tombe (dance → dancing, write → writing), et une consonne après une voyelle courte se double (swim → swimming).

Chaque phrase contient une faute. Trouve-la et corrige-la. I like speak English. I dislike to clean the board. I like play in the playground. I like speaking English. I dislike cleaning the board. I like playing in the playground.

Traduis en anglais. J'aime l'anglais. Je n'aime pas nettoyer la cour de récréation. J'aime aller au jardin de l'école. I like English. I dislike cleaning the playground. I like going to the school garden.

Deux amies parlent de ce qu'elles aiment à l'école. Joue la scène. Aya: Hi Karniella! Do you like our new school? Karniella: Yes, I do. I like the library. I like reading there. Aya: Me too! And I like playing in the playground. Karniella: I dislike cleaning the classroom on Fridays! Aya: Ha ha, me too. But I like working in the school garden. Do you like your school? → Yes, I do. / No, I don't. What do you like doing at school? → I like …ing … What do you dislike doing? → I dislike …ing …
La terminaison -ing se prononce « ing », le g est à peine audible : speaking, reading. playground : l'accent est sur PLAY. secretary : « SÉ-kre-tri », trois syllabes seulement.
Le vocabulaire de la Session 2 et la règle like / dislike.

quiz.question: It's the place where students go to play and practise sports. What is it?
quiz.explication: A playground: it's the place where students go to play and practise sports.

quiz.question: It's the work place of the secretary. What is it?
quiz.explication: A secretary's office: it's the work place of the secretary.

quiz.question: Where do students go to grow vegetables?
quiz.explication: A school garden: it's the place where students go to grow vegetables.

quiz.question: Après « like », comment écrit-on le verbe qui suit ?
quiz.explication: like + V-ing : I like speaking English. Jamais « I like speak » ni « I like to speak » dans cette leçon.

quiz.question: Quelle phrase est CORRECTE ?
quiz.explication: like + verbe + -ing → I like speaking English.

quiz.question: Complète : « I dislike ____ the board. »
quiz.explication: dislike + V-ing → I dislike cleaning the board. C'est la même règle qu'avec like.

quiz.question: « I like English. » — quelle construction est utilisée ici ?
quiz.explication: English est un nom : c'est la construction like + noun.

quiz.question: Laquelle de ces phrases exprime un DISLIKE correctement ?
Complete: I like (swim) ___.
quiz.explication: Swim → swimming: the m is doubled.

quiz.question: Complete: She dislikes (dance) ___.
quiz.explication: Dance → dancing: the final e disappears.

quiz.question: Which sentence is correct?
quiz.explication: Like + verb-ing: I like speaking English.

quiz.question: Comment dit-on « Je n'aime pas les chiens » ?
quiz.explication: Dislike + nom au pluriel : I dislike dogs.
